legal.notice.title: Before your first match
legal.notice.lede: Zap is a personal, non-profit project run by one private individual. Here is what happens to your data, in a few lines:
legal.notice.who.label: Who is responsible
legal.notice.what.label: What is kept
legal.notice.what.text: A random code for this browser, an internal pseudonym, your nickname if you pick one, the moves of each match with the time each decision took, and counters of your way of playing. Your name, email and IP address are not kept.
legal.notice.why.label: Why
legal.notice.why.text: To run the game, keep bots out, train the AI and build the data page. The legal basis is legitimate interest (LGPD, art. 7, IX). The counters of your way of playing only show you how Zap reads you. During a match the AI reads only the plays of that match and keeps nothing of them. The public ranking, once it exists, will only list people who ask to join.
legal.notice.keep.label: For how long
legal.notice.keep.text: Until you delete it, or until 12 months without playing. Match records stay, but with no link to you.
legal.notice.rights.label: Your rights
legal.notice.rights.text: Those in art. 18 of the LGPD, Brazil's data protection law. On the You page you can see, download and delete your data at any time, and opt out of the open data.
legal.notice.contact.label: Contact
legal.notice.contact.ifContact: {contact}. You get an answer within 15 days.
legal.notice.contact.ifNoContact: There is no contact address yet. Requests are made on the You page and take effect right away.
legal.notice.share.label: Who else gets it
legal.notice.share.text: Cloudflare hosts the site and runs the human check. Once there are 1,000 matches with people, matches with no link to who played will be published on GitHub as open data.
legal.notice.where.label: Where
legal.notice.where.text: Rooms run in the United States, so your data is transferred there.
legal.notice.age.label: Age
legal.notice.ads.label: Ads
legal.notice.ads.text: Only non-personalized ads, and only if you accept them. Google uses cookies to show and measure the ads. People who refuse play the same, without ads.
legal.notice.more: The details are in Privacy and in Terms of use. By going on, you accept the terms.
legal.privacy.description: What Zap keeps, why, for how long, and how to download or delete your data.
legal.privacy.title: Privacy
legal.privacy.lede: Zap is a personal, non-profit project run by one private individual. This page explains what Zap keeps about the people who play, why, for how long, and what you can do about it.
legal.privacy.who.title: Who is responsible for the data
legal.privacy.who.p1: Andrei Ludescher, who runs Zap, decides how the data is used. Under the LGPD, Brazil's data protection law, he is the controller.
legal.privacy.who.ifNoContact: There is no contact address yet. Everything you can do with your data is on the You page.
legal.privacy.account.title: No sign-up
legal.privacy.account.p1: Zap does not ask for your name, email or a password. On your first match, this browser gets a random secret code, kept in a cookie that only Zap's server receives. The server keeps only a fingerprint of that code (a hash), never the code itself.
legal.privacy.account.p2: Next to that fingerprint sits an internal pseudonym: another random code, kept in Zap's database and shown only to you, on the You page. The "You against Zap" page keeps a copy of it in this browser, next to the copies of your matches.
legal.privacy.account.p3: Match records carry only the match number and the seat number. The link between your pseudonym and your seats lives in a separate table. When you delete your data, that link is gone, and nothing in the records points to you anymore.
legal.privacy.account.p4: If you clear this browser's data, you lose access to your history. To avoid that, save a recovery code on the You page.
legal.privacy.collected.title: What Zap keeps
legal.privacy.collected.li1: The fingerprint of this browser's code and the internal pseudonym.
legal.privacy.collected.li2: That you said you are 18 or older, and when. Your birth year never leaves the browser.
legal.privacy.collected.li3: Your nickname, if you pick one. People in the same room can see it.
legal.privacy.collected.li4: Your choices on the You page: staying out of the open data and not having the game adapt to you.
legal.privacy.collected.li5: Dates: when this browser started playing, the last time it played, and the last human check, with how many matches since then.
legal.privacy.collected.li6: Which matches and seats were yours, whether your seat had the verified human badge, and how many matches you abandoned.
legal.privacy.collected.li7: The moves of each match, how long you took on each decision, and whether a move was made automatically because time ran out. These records contain nothing that points to you.
legal.privacy.collected.li8: Reports you made, and marks of suspected automated play on this browser, with the review of each one.
legal.privacy.collected.li9: Rooms you created or joined, while they are open, and 15 minute pauses for sending too many messages.
legal.privacy.collected.li10: The fingerprint of your recovery code, if you create one.
legal.privacy.collected.li11: Counters of your way of playing, added up after each match and kept apart by variant and number of players: how often you call truco, run, accept, raise, play face down and bluff, the strength of the cards you show after calling truco, whether your signals tell the truth, and how long you take to decide. The You page shows their reading. With "Don't adapt to me" on, none of this is kept. Your rating, once it exists, is kept too.
legal.privacy.notCollected.title: What Zap does not keep
legal.privacy.notCollected.p1: Your name, email, phone number, location, birth year or contacts. There is no free chat: only canned phrases and the game's signals.
legal.privacy.notCollected.p2: Zap does not record your IP address. To curb abuse it uses a fingerprint of the IP made with a key that changes every day, and that fingerprint is not recorded either. The server's access logs are switched off.
legal.privacy.notCollected.p3: There are no ads or trackers today. If that changes, this page changes first and the notice shows up again.
legal.privacy.browser.title: In your browser
legal.privacy.browser.p1: Two cookies, both needed to play: this browser's secret code, and a pass that lasts 2 hours after the human check.
legal.privacy.browser.p2: The browser also keeps the following until you clear the site's data, without sending it to the server or anywhere else:
legal.privacy.browser.li2: That you declared being 18 or older, and the version of the notice you read, so the question and the notice do not come back. Deleting your data on the You page also removes both from this browser.
legal.privacy.browser.li3: Your last choice on the Play page: mode and variant.
legal.privacy.browser.li4: Your settings: "Four-color deck", "Sound and vibration", "Single key shortcuts" and "Mute phrases and signals from others".
legal.privacy.browser.li5: Which first-match hints (vira, manilha and tentos) you have already seen, so they do not show up again.
legal.privacy.browser.p3: Until you close the tab, it also keeps, without sending them to the server:
legal.privacy.browser.li6: The last room code, for the button that takes you back to that room.
legal.privacy.browser.li7: When Zap has reached its limit for the day or the month, the time when matches start again. The page uses it for one hour at most, so it does not ask the server on every click.
legal.privacy.browser.p4: If you open the "You against Zap" page, this browser also keeps copies of your matches and a copy of your pseudonym, in a database of the browser itself (IndexedDB). That way the page opens faster and does not download a match it already has. These copies are not sent to the server or anywhere else.
legal.privacy.purposes.title: What the data is for, and the legal basis
legal.privacy.purposes.li1: Playing, opening rooms and getting back to the table after a dropped connection: browser code, pseudonym, nickname and seats. Basis: legitimate interest (LGPD, art. 7, IX), using only what is needed.
legal.privacy.purposes.li2: Keeping bots out: the human check result, decision times and how many matches you play. In each training cycle, the training server looks for patterns of automated play in the daily export, and a mark takes your matches out of training at once. Basis: legitimate interest.
legal.privacy.purposes.li3: History, rating and the "You against Zap" page: your matches, read by your browser. The rating and the numbers on that page are computed on your device, and the server keeps no rating. Basis: legitimate interest.
legal.privacy.purposes.li4: Training the AI and building the data page: the moves, with nothing that points to you. When a new AI version comes out, for two weeks a share of quick play matches, drawn at random, keeps the previous version, so the two can be compared by their results; the figures are shown only with 20 or more people in each group. Basis: legitimate interest.
legal.privacy.purposes.li5: Showing you how Zap reads your way of playing, on the You page and on "You against Zap": that is all the counters of your style are for. During a match, the AI reads only the plays everyone at the table saw in that match; it keeps nothing of that reading and forgets it when the match ends. Basis: legitimate interest, with the "Don't adapt to me" switch.
legal.privacy.purposes.li6: Open data: moves with nothing that points to you, under the rules described below. Basis: legitimate interest, with the "Keep me out of open data" switch.
legal.privacy.purposes.li7: Public ranking, once it exists: nickname and rating band. Basis: consent. Only people who ask are listed, and you can leave at any time.
legal.privacy.purposes.p1: Legitimate interest means using data for what you would expect from a game like this one, weighed against your rights. The balancing test for each use is published in the repository.
legal.privacy.retention.title: How long data is kept
legal.privacy.retention.li1: Browser code, pseudonym, nickname, the counters of your style and your history, that is, which matches were yours: until you delete them, or until 12 months without playing. The rating is not kept on the server: it is computed on your device each time you open "You against Zap".
legal.privacy.retention.li2: Copies of your matches and of the pseudonym kept in this browser by the "You against Zap" page: until you delete your data on the You page, use the "Forget the games stored on this device" button or clear the site's data in your browser.
legal.privacy.retention.li3: Match records: kept with no time limit and no link to any person, to train the AI and for the data page.
legal.privacy.retention.li4: Daily export for the training server: your seats show up with a group code drawn again every day, with no pseudonym. Only Zap's database knows whose each code is, and only for 30 days, to apply marks of automated play; a mark not yet reviewed keeps its code until it is reviewed, and a reviewed mark keeps it for 30 more days. Each export is kept for 7 days. The training server keeps only the newest one, the tables of the latest training cycle and of the daily check of a new version, with the same codes, and the list of marks it made, for up to 400 days; earlier cycles keep no codes, even when a cycle fails.
legal.privacy.retention.li6: Marks of suspected automated play: 12 months after review.
legal.privacy.retention.li7: A room's state (seats and the match in progress): deleted when the room closes or after 24 hours without use.
legal.privacy.retention.li9: Automatic database backups: gone within 30 days.
legal.privacy.retention.li10: Open data already published: permanent, since a release cannot be pulled back.
legal.privacy.sharing.title: Who the data is shared with
legal.privacy.sharing.p1: Cloudflare hosts the site, the rooms and the database, and runs the human check (Turnstile). Like any service on the internet, it receives your IP address to deliver the pages. The check runs in your browser and reads signals from it to tell people from bots; Cloudflare handles that data under its own privacy policy. Zap does not send your IP address to the check.
legal.privacy.sharing.p2: GitHub: once there are 1,000 matches with people, Zap builds open data packages and publishes them on GitHub, under the CC BY 4.0 license, with each new AI version. The maintainer publishes the first package by hand, after checking what is in it; the later ones go out on their own, under the same rules. Nothing in them points to a person. Each match gets a new code, and no row links two matches by the same person. Dates show only the week of the year. Decision times are grouped in half second bands. Each mix of week, variant and mode is published only if it covers 20 or more different people. Separately, summed style figures are published: the mean and the spread of each figure over 20 or more people with 50 matches or more, with no link to the matches and no row for a single person.
legal.privacy.sharing.p3: If you delete your data or switch on "Keep me out of open data", you are left out of future releases: a package goes out only if it was built from the newest export, of that day or the day before. Releases already out cannot be pulled back, because anyone may have copied them.
legal.privacy.sharing.p4: Nobody else gets your data, and Zap does not sell data. Public pages show only figures for groups, never for one person.
legal.privacy.transfer.title: Transfer outside Brazil
legal.privacy.transfer.p1: Cloudflare does not offer this kind of room server in South America, so Zap's rooms run in eastern North America, in the United States. The database and the match records may also be stored outside Brazil. Your data is therefore transferred to the United States.
legal.privacy.rights.title: Your rights and how to use them
legal.privacy.rights.p1: The LGPD, in art. 18, gives you these rights, among others. On Zap they work like this:
legal.privacy.rights.li1: Confirm that Zap holds data about you, see it and take it elsewhere: download all of it as a JSON file on the You page.
legal.privacy.rights.li2: Correct it: change your nickname on the You page. The rest is a record of what happened in your matches.
legal.privacy.rights.li3: Delete it: on the You page, right away, after a confirmation.
legal.privacy.rights.li4: Object to a use: the "Keep me out of open data" and "Don't adapt to me" switches on the You page.
legal.privacy.rights.li5: Withdraw consent for the public ranking, once it exists: just leave it, at any time.
legal.privacy.rights.li6: Ask for a review of a mark of suspected automated play: a person reviews every mark before it has any lasting effect.
legal.privacy.rights.li7: Know who your data is shared with: it is on this page.
legal.privacy.rights.li8: Complain to Brazil's National Data Protection Authority (ANPD).
legal.privacy.rights.ifContact: For anything else, write to {contact}. You get an answer within 15 days.
legal.privacy.rights.ifNoContact: There is no contact address yet, so requests are made on the You page and take effect right away.
legal.privacy.rights.p2: If you lose access to your history, for example after clearing the browser or changing devices, use your recovery code on the You page. Without it there is no way to tell which matches were yours: Zap has no other way to recognize you.
legal.privacy.minors.title: People under 18
legal.privacy.minors.p1: Zap is only for people 18 or older, by self-declaration: before the first match, the site asks for your birth year. People under 18 can read the rules and the data page but cannot play, and nothing about them reaches the server.
legal.privacy.minors.p2: If someone under 18 played anyway, delete the data on the You page, in the same browser. Parents and guardians can do this too.
legal.privacy.minors.ifContact: You can also write to {contact} and the data will be deleted.
legal.privacy.minors.p3: Even with the minimum age, Zap has no betting, purchases, free chat or ads, and it has buttons to report someone and to mute others.
legal.privacy.security.title: Security
legal.privacy.security.p1: Connections are encrypted (HTTPS). This browser's secret code sits in a cookie that page scripts cannot read, and the server keeps only fingerprints of codes. Only the maintainer has access to the account where the data is stored.
legal.privacy.security.p2: If an incident could bring you real risk or harm, it will be reported on this page and to the ANPD.
legal.privacy.changes.title: Changes
legal.privacy.changes.p1: If this page changes in a way that matters, the notice shows up again before your next match. The version date is at the top.
legal.terms.description: The rules for using Zap: minimum age, conduct in rooms, reports, and what Zap offers.
legal.terms.title: Terms of use
legal.terms.lede: Zap is a personal, non-profit project run by one private individual. By playing, you accept these terms.
legal.terms.about.title: What Zap is
legal.terms.about.p1: A free truco game in the browser, against an AI that learns from the people who play. There are no bets, prizes or purchases, and no money is at stake.
legal.terms.about.p2: AIs always show their name and character. The AI gets new versions over time, so its strength can change.
legal.terms.age.title: Minimum age
legal.terms.age.p1: You must be 18 or older to play. You declare your age yourself, and declaring a false age breaks these terms.
legal.terms.account.title: No account
legal.terms.account.p1: There is no sign-up. Zap recognizes this browser by a secret code kept in a cookie. A recovery code gives access to your history, so keep it to yourself.
legal.terms.conduct.title: Conduct
legal.terms.conduct.li1: Use your nickname, canned phrases or signals to offend, harass, threaten or discriminate against anyone.
legal.terms.conduct.li2: Pick a nickname that is offensive or that pretends to be someone else.
legal.terms.conduct.li3: Play with bots, scripts or any kind of automation, or let a program play for you.
legal.terms.conduct.li4: Try to see hidden cards, disrupt the server, flood it with messages or get around the human check.
legal.terms.report.title: Reporting and muting
legal.terms.report.p1: In the table menu, "Report" lets you pick a seat and a reason: nickname, phrases or signals, cheating, or something else.
legal.terms.report.p2: A reported nickname is hidden right away and shows as "Player 3", with the seat number, until it is reviewed or changed.
legal.terms.report.p3: If you would rather not see anything from others, use "Mute phrases and signals from others", also in the table menu.
legal.terms.consequences.title: What can happen
legal.terms.consequences.p1: If you break these rules, your nickname may be removed, you may be left out of the ranking and of AI training, or you may be stopped from playing. Sending too many messages pauses the browser for 15 minutes, right away. Marks of automated play are reviewed by a person before they have any lasting effect.
legal.terms.service.title: The service
legal.terms.service.p1: Zap is offered as it is, with no promise that it will always be online. Matches can drop, rooms expire after 24 hours without use, and on busy days Zap may stop starting matches until the next day. Anything here can change or end, since this is a personal project.
legal.terms.service.p2: Zap's code is open under the MIT license. The cards, the texts, the data page and the open data use the CC BY 4.0 license.
legal.terms.data.title: Your data
legal.terms.data.p1: How Zap handles your data is explained on the Privacy page.
legal.terms.changes.title: Changes
legal.terms.changes.p1: When these terms change, the new version shows up before your next match.
legal.terms.changes.p2: These terms are governed by Brazilian law.
legal.verify.description: How Zap tries to tell people from bots, what the verified human badge means, and why it is not a guarantee.
legal.verify.title: How we verify
legal.verify.lede: Zap learns from the people who play, so it needs to know, as well as it can, which moves come from people. This page explains how that works and where it falls short.
legal.verify.check.title: The human check
legal.verify.check.p1: When you start a match, or create or join a room, the site runs a Cloudflare check called Turnstile. Most of the time it passes on its own; sometimes it asks for a click.
legal.verify.check.p2: Zap's server confirms the result with Cloudflare. Each result works once, for 5 minutes, and only for this site. Your IP address is not sent along with it.
legal.verify.check.p3: When the check passes, this browser gets a signed pass that lasts 2 hours or 10 matches, whichever runs out first. After that, the check comes back.
legal.verify.seal.title: The verified human badge
legal.verify.seal.p1: The badge shows next to a person while their browser's pass is valid: up to 2 hours or 10 matches after the check. They must also have no mark of suspected automated play.
legal.verify.seal.p2: AIs never get the badge: they always show their name and character.
legal.verify.seal.p3: The badge is not a guarantee. A well made bot can pass the check.
legal.verify.limits.title: Limits
legal.verify.limits.li1: Each connection can send about 4 messages per second, with some room for short bursts. Going over that disconnects it and pauses the browser for 15 minutes.
legal.verify.limits.li3: Up to 3 rooms with friends open at the same time per browser.
legal.verify.signs.title: Signs of automated play
legal.verify.signs.p1: In each training cycle, Zap looks for patterns that people rarely show: decision times that are too steady, play around the clock, unusual volume, and identical sequences of moves. The search uses only the daily export, where each browser shows up with a new group code every day.
legal.verify.signs.p2: A marked browser leaves AI training at once, and the ranking for the time being. A person reviews every mark. A mark lifted in a review never comes back from the same matches: only matches played after the review can lead to a new mark, and from the same sign only after 90 days. A person reviews every new mark too. The You page shows whether there is a mark on your browser.
legal.verify.signs.ifContact: To ask for a review, write to {contact}.
legal.verify.signs.ifNoContact: Every mark is reviewed, even without a request.
legal.verify.training.title: Why this matters for the AI
legal.verify.training.p1: Not every move counts the same in training. Each browser gets a trust weight based on the check, its history and abandoned matches, and no browser can make up more than 2% of the data. Automatic moves, made when time ran out, are left out.
legal.verify.training.p2: Even if a bot gets through, it cannot change the AI much: a new version goes live only if it beats the current one.
legal.you.description: Your history on Zap, your nickname and choices, and how to download or delete your data.
legal.you.title: You
legal.you.lede: Everything Zap keeps about this browser, and what you can do with it.
legal.you.empty: This browser has not played yet. Zap keeps nothing about it.
legal.you.loadFailed: Could not load your data. Try again.
legal.you.device.title: No account
legal.you.device.text: Zap recognizes you by a secret code kept in this browser. If you clear the site's data, you lose your history. To avoid that, create a recovery code.
legal.you.stored.title: What Zap keeps
legal.you.stored.pseudonymHelp: A random code that links you to your matches inside Zap's database. Only you see it, here, and it never goes into match records.
legal.you.stored.adult: Said you are 18 or older on
legal.you.stored.flagHelp: A mark means that something in the way this browser plays looked automated. While it stands, your matches stay out of AI training and the ranking. A person reviews every mark.
legal.you.stored.flagReview.ifContact: To ask for a review, write to {contact}.
legal.you.stored.flagReview.ifNoContact: Every mark is reviewed, even without a request.
legal.you.matches.title: Your matches
legal.you.nickname.title: Nickname
legal.you.nickname.help: 2 to 20 characters: letters, digits and spaces. People in the same room can see it. Without a nickname, you show as Player and your seat number.
legal.you.nickname.label: Your nickname
legal.you.nickname.bad: That nickname cannot be used. Try another one.
legal.you.nickname.hidden: Your nickname was reported and is hidden until it is reviewed. Meanwhile, you show as Player and your seat number. A new nickname shows right away.
legal.you.prefs.title: Your choices
legal.you.prefs.openData: Keep me out of open data
legal.you.prefs.openDataHelp: Your matches are left out of future open data releases. Releases already out cannot be pulled back.
legal.you.prefs.noAdaptHelp: When it is on, Zap deletes the counters of your style right away and keeps no new ones, and from your next match the AI does not read the plays of anyone at your table, yours included. In our tests that play is slightly weaker, in your favour.
legal.you.download.title: Download my data
legal.you.download.text: A JSON file with everything Zap keeps about this browser and the full records of your matches. The file is put together here, in your browser.
legal.you.download.failed: The download stopped partway. Try again.
legal.you.delete.title: Delete my data
legal.you.delete.text: Deletes right away everything that links you to your matches: this browser's code, the pseudonym, the nickname, your choices, your history, the counters of your style, the reports you made and the marks about you. Match records stay, with no link to you. In this browser, it also deletes the copies the "You against Zap" page kept.
legal.you.delete.more: Reports other people made about you stay, but without the link to you. Automatic database backups are gone within 30 days. Open data already published cannot be pulled back.
legal.you.delete.confirmText: Your history goes away for good, even with a recovery code. If you play again, you start from scratch.
legal.you.delete.check: Confirm you are a person to delete.
legal.you.delete.failed: Could not delete right now. Try again.
legal.you.recovery.title: Recovery code
legal.you.recovery.text: With this code you can open your history in another browser or on another device. Anyone with the code gets your history, so keep it to yourself.
legal.you.recovery.replaces: A new code cancels the previous one.
legal.you.recovery.once: This code shows only now. Write it down or copy it before you leave.
legal.you.recover.title: Recover on another device
legal.you.recover.text: Type the recovery code you created in another browser. This browser takes over your history, and the other one loses access. Each code works once; after that, create a new one.
legal.you.recover.label: Recovery code
legal.you.recover.hint: 20 letters and digits, in groups of 5.
legal.you.recover.check: Confirm you are a person to recover.
legal.you.recover.bad: That code was not found. Check it and try again.
legal.you.recover.done: Done. This browser now has your history.
legal.you.recover.replaceWarn: If this browser already has matches, they move into the recovered history. To delete them instead, use "Delete my data" first.
